report.source_text: A transabdominal ultrasound (USG)-guided aspiration of the fluid was done and sent for geneXpert®, cell cytology, cell block, and culture (bacterial/fungal/tubercular). GeneXpert® was negative for tuberculosis. The fluid cytology was negative for malignant cells and the cell block showed reactive mesothelial cells and neutrophils. The microbiological reports revealed a sterile bacterial culture. On fungal culture, fungal elements were seen, which were grown on Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) (Bruker Daltonics, Germany), which showed them to be Curvularia lunata.

clinician.final_diagnosis: fungal peritonitis by Curvularia lunata and later multidrug-resistant (MDR) tuberculosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old female presented with irregular menstruation, abdominal distension, and lower abdominal pain. Initial MRI showed extensive peritoneal thickening, ascites, and multiloculated adnexal lesions, raising suspicion for ovarian malignancy. Initial workup showed elevated ESR, normal other tumor markers, and negative IGRA. USG-guided aspiration of ascites fluid revealed negative GeneXpert for TB, negative cytology for malignancy, sterile bacterial culture, but fungal culture identified Curvularia lunata, confirming fungal peritonitis. She was treated with oral itraconazole. Follow-up CECT showed persistent adnexal masses and peritoneal thickening, but a second aspiration's fungal culture was negative. After 6 weeks of itraconazole, she was symptomatically improved, and repeat MRI showed near-total resolution of masses. Itraconazole was stopped. Two months later, she presented with chest wall swelling and weight loss. A CT scan showed miliary tuberculosis and a cold abscess in the chest wall, leading to the diagnosis of tuberculosis, which was later identified as multidrug-resistant.

Diagnosis of fungal peritonitis by Curvularia lunata from ascites fluid culture.
Treatment with oral itraconazole led to symptomatic improvement and resolution of masses on MRI.
Later presentation with chest wall swelling and weight loss, with CT scan showing miliary tuberculosis and cold abscess in the chest wall.
